run.method: baseline-blind adversarial anti-brand grammar and citation-stewardship repertory grid
run.brief: Complete task: Create run id run-19d-form-counterclaim-citation. Generator: kind model, name "form saturation generator B counterclaim/citation", provider openai, model gpt-5.5, reasoning_effort high, agent_id null. Method: "baseline-blind adversarial anti-brand grammar and citation-stewardship repertory grid". parent_run_ids []. Run notes must include "challenge_wave: form-saturation-b", "independent baseline-blind generation", "cell 8: counter-claims", and "cell 10: eponym-citation-architecture". Read only identity/atlas.json, identity/schema/portfolio.schema.json, README.md, docs/DSEX_PHILOSOPHY.md, and docs/RESEARCH_LANDSCAPE.md. Do NOT read identity/inbox/*, identity/reports/*, registry/enrichments/assessments, candidate lists, leaders, scores, or favorites. Do not browse, search availability, rank, filter, deduplicate, or suppress adverse or malformed conceptual output. Product boundary: this is a pre-release Elixir/OTP library for declared, callable, measurable, optimizable LM programs, with a credible runtime-contracted textual/artifact optimization horizon spanning instructions, demonstrations, tool descriptions, retrieval policies, playbooks, schemas, code fragments, and configuration. It is not an official DSPy port, static proof system, universal agent OS, provider SDK, guaranteed autonomous self-improvement engine, safety product, standards body, institute, or universal platform. Create a valid schema_version 1, atlas_version 1 portfolio with exactly 20 candidates and contiguous ordinals 1..20. Ordinals 1..10 are challenge_cell: counter-claims. Ordinals 11..20 are challenge_cell: eponym-citation-architecture. Each cell has exactly two wildcard true. Every candidate must have non-null pronunciation and grammar, honest etymology or explicit coined/no-source text, substantive rationale, nonempty valid territories, strategies, audience_lenses, and architecture_lenses, known_concerns, and notes. Every notes array must contain separate strings for challenge_wave: form-saturation-b, challenge_cell, form_mechanism, stance, scope, code_projection, current_embodiment, and horizon_embodiment. Every eponym/citation candidate must additionally have citation_stewardship. code_projection must truthfully show hex, otp, module, mix, config, and telemetry forms using conventional valid Elixir/Hex lowercase identifiers where possible; if a surface cannot produce one honestly, use null and explain it in concerns rather than inventing invalid code. For each 10-candidate cell, exact stance counts are 5 affirmative, 3 ambivalent, 2 adverse. For each cell, exact scope counts are 4 current, 4 horizon, 2 both. Pair every hostile false assurance, institutional overclaim, conquest/control posture, or uncited prestige borrowing with an affirmative alternative in the same cell and record the paired ordinal in notes. Counter-claims must explore real grammatical mechanisms that challenge what a software identity is allowed to promise: imperatives, questions, bounded declarations, refusal/abstention, negation with scope, hedges, inversion, anti-slogans, role/category grammar, and deliberately hostile false assurances. Affirmative entries must remain usable identities, not only critiques. They must not let a name warrant safety, privacy, fairness, consent, proof, correctness, reliability, accessibility, healing, or improvement. Eponym/citation architecture must explore accurate attributed names, non-eponymic controls, citation-bearing research-series structures, historical objects or practices with documented attribution duties, deliberately adverse prestige borrowing, and role/system architecture. Do not fabricate relationships, permissions, endorsements, Indigenous/sacred provenance, or historical claims. Every citation_stewardship note must state the attribution duty, likely ambiguity or harm, and whether the form is viable without the person's name. Prefer public historical figures or clearly documented terms; avoid living-person endorsement implications. At least four entries in this cell must be non-eponymic controls or architectures that carry citations without turning a person into the product master brand. Use only atlas IDs. Include current and horizon embodiments even when one is intentionally unavailable. Keep architecture implications truthful. Validate JSON shape, atlas ID membership, exact candidate/ordinal/wildcard/stance/scope counts, required notes, code projections, and citation stewardship with jq before reporting. Do not run a global checkpoint while other files are in progress.

candidates.grammar: Imperative phrase that tells builders to restrict action to evaluated program boundaries.
candidates.rationale: This is a usable identity because it makes the library's call boundary and metric discipline memorable without claiming correctness or guaranteed improvement. It can name a project, manual section, or campaign architecture for DSEx-style programs that are declared, called, evaluated, and optimized only where evidence is available.
candidates.etymology: Plain English phrase; coined here with no external source claim.
known_concerns: Long as a master brand and stronger as a campaign or doctrine identity.
The imperative could sound prescriptive if isolated from examples and limits.
notes: code_projection: hex=call_measure; otp=:call_measure; module=CallMeasure; mix=mix call_measure.eval; config=:call_measure; telemetry=[:call_measure, :program, :stop]
current_embodiment: A current DSEx identity for declared programs whose calls, predictions, metrics, and traces are explicit.

horizon_embodiment: Extends to artifact optimization only where instructions, demonstrations, tool descriptions, retrieval policies, playbooks, schemas, code fragments, or configuration have measurable evaluation boundaries.

candidates.grammar: Negated noun phrase with scoped denial of formal verification claims.
candidates.rationale: The surface is stark but usable for a technical identity that wins trust by refusing an inflated warranty. It protects the product boundary around runtime contracts, tests, examples, traces, and metrics while leaving room for rigorous evaluation and optimizer lineage.
candidates.etymology: Plain English phrase; coined here with no external source claim.
known_concerns: Negative affect may reduce approachability for newcomers.
Needs an affirmative descriptor nearby so the project is not defined only by refusal.
notes: code_projection: hex=not_a_proof; otp=:not_a_proof; module=NotAProof; mix=mix not_a_proof.check; config=:not_a_proof; telemetry=[:not_a_proof, :eval, :stop]
current_embodiment: A current boundary identity for DSEx as callable and measurable Elixir code rather than a static proof system.
horizon_embodiment: Can remain a warning label for optimizer campaigns over arbitrary textual artifacts, especially when promotion gates are empirical rather than formal.

candidates.grammar: Subordinate question-like clause that foregrounds refusal and non-action as part of program behavior.
candidates.rationale: This name makes abstention a first-class program capability without promising safety, consent, or moral correctness. It fits DSEx because signatures, adapters, metrics, and tools can encode when a program returns no answer, asks for more context, or declines an action.
candidates.etymology: Plain English phrase; coined here with no external source claim.
known_concerns: Sounds like a policy module unless paired with program examples.
Abstention can be overread as safety assurance; copy must keep it behavioral and testable.
notes: code_projection: hex=abstain_when; otp=:abstain_when; module=AbstainWhen; mix=mix abstain_when.eval; config=:abstain_when; telemetry=[:abstain_when, :decision, :stop]
current_embodiment: Current DSEx programs can model refusal or missing-output cases through signatures, adapters, metrics, and tool boundaries.
horizon_embodiment: Horizon artifact optimization can include refusal policies and playbooks as optimizable text parameters only after they are evaluated against explicit examples.

candidates.grammar: Bounded declaration that narrows the referent to program objects and their runtime contracts.
candidates.rationale: The name resists platform inflation while still giving a crisp identity to an Elixir library for signatures, programs, predictions, metrics, and optimizers. It can sit on current DSEx APIs and later on artifact-parameter campaigns without implying a universal agent OS.
candidates.etymology: Plain English phrase; coined here with no external source claim.
known_concerns: May underplay evaluation, optimization, and operations unless supported by descriptors.
Could be too generic for search without a distinctive package name.
notes: code_projection: hex=only_program; otp=:only_program; module=OnlyProgram; mix=mix only_program.run; config=:only_program; telemetry=[:only_program, :call, :stop]
current_embodiment: Current embodiment is a library identity that keeps claims attached to declared callable programs.
horizon_embodiment: Horizon embodiment keeps artifact optimization inside program-like contracts rather than expanding into a universal platform claim.

candidates.grammar: Hedged comparative plus evidentiary modifier.
candidates.rationale: This identity names optimizer humility: a DSEx campaign may improve a program, fail to improve it, or trade off dimensions, so the result must be measured. It is affirmative because it gives teams a responsible way to talk about optimization without guaranteeing autonomous improvement.
candidates.etymology: Plain English phrase; coined here with no external source claim.
known_concerns: The hedge may weaken commercial force.
Needs careful grammar so 'better' is always tied to a metric and comparison set.
notes: code_projection: hex=maybe_measured; otp=:maybe_measured; module=MaybeMeasured; mix=mix maybe_measured.promote; config=:maybe_measured; telemetry=[:maybe_measured, :optimizer, :stop]
current_embodiment: Current embodiment can label evaluation and optimizer examples that report scores instead of promises.
horizon_embodiment: Horizon embodiment can govern artifact optimization campaigns where promotion requires evidence, uncertainty, and held-out checks.

candidates.grammar: Inversion and contrastive negation that puts executable structure before marketing promise.
candidates.rationale: This is an ambivalent but valuable master-line candidate: it is memorable and truthful, yet slightly defensive. It challenges identity grammar by making the product's warrant come from declared structures, traces, and metrics rather than from a reassuring name.
candidates.etymology: Plain English contrast phrase; coined here with no external source claim.
known_concerns: Defensive tone may become tiring as a primary identity.
The word promise still introduces warranty associations that copy must carefully narrow.
notes: code_projection: hex=program_not_promise; otp=:program_not_promise; module=ProgramNotPromise; mix=mix program_not_promise.audit; config=:program_not_promise; telemetry=[:program_not_promise, :trace, :stop]
current_embodiment: Current embodiment is a slogan-like identity for DSEx APIs where program values and tests carry the claim.
horizon_embodiment: Horizon embodiment can still fit broader artifact parameters, but only if the artifact remains inside versioned program contracts.

candidates.grammar: Conquest imperative with command/control posture.
candidates.rationale: This hostile-form candidate is intentionally ambivalent because it is legible to automation buyers but distorts DSEx into domination over stochastic model behavior. It is useful only as a warning against names that make runtime uncertainty sound conquered.
candidates.etymology: Plain English phrase; coined here with no external source claim.
known_concerns: Overstates control over model behavior and may imply guarantees the library cannot make.
Conquest grammar conflicts with bounded tools, evaluation, and refusal.
notes: code_projection: hex=command_model; otp=:command_model; module=CommandModel; mix=mix command_model.run; config=:command_model; telemetry=[:command_model, :control, :stop]
current_embodiment: Current embodiment is intentionally compromised because DSEx can call and evaluate programs but cannot command model behavior into reliability.
horizon_embodiment: Horizon embodiment remains risky for artifact optimization because it frames search and feedback as control rather than measured selection.

candidates.grammar: Role/category grammar using a concrete limit object as modifier.
candidates.rationale: The phrase is ambivalent because the brake metaphor is accessible but could oversimplify runtime limits. It keeps the software identity honest by requiring call boundaries, evaluation stops, timeouts, and promotion gates to be part of the name's grammar.
candidates.etymology: Plain English phrase; coined here with no external source claim.
known_concerns: Mechanical metaphor may imply deterministic stopping across all external systems.
Better as a subsystem or operations doctrine than a master brand.
notes: code_projection: hex=program_brake; otp=:program_brake; module=ProgramBrake; mix=mix program_brake.check; config=:program_brake; telemetry=[:program_brake, :gate, :stop]
current_embodiment: Current embodiment maps to deterministic tests, explicit runtime configuration, and gates around calls.
horizon_embodiment: Horizon embodiment maps to optimizer stop policies, rollback, and promotion gates for textual artifacts.

candidates.rationale: This adverse candidate documents a forbidden identity form: the name asserts safety and answer quality before any product, evaluator, or deployment context can support it. It is useful as negative coverage for the grammar that DSEx must not adopt.

known_concerns: False safety assurance; should not be used as product identity.

horizon_embodiment: Horizon embodiment is unavailable because artifact optimization cannot make universal safety guarantees.

candidates.grammar: Deliberately hostile false assurance using proof verb and universal quantifier.
candidates.rationale: This adverse candidate captures the exact identity trap around formal-sounding software names. DSEx can validate schemas, run tests, evaluate metrics, and compare optimizer outputs, but it is not a proof system and should not use grammar that says it proves prompts.
candidates.etymology: Plain English phrase; coined here as an adverse no-source anti-pattern.
known_concerns: False proof claim and prompt-centric scope distortion.
The valid code form would still encode an invalid product promise and should remain a negative example.

current_embodiment: Current embodiment is unavailable because DSEx does not prove prompts or programs.
horizon_embodiment: Horizon embodiment is unavailable because broader artifact optimization still relies on empirical contracts, not universal proof.

candidates.grammar: Eponymic technical compound naming traceable multi-objective selection rather than a product master.
candidates.rationale: Pareto is a public historical attribution widely used in optimization vocabulary, and the word trace keeps the identity tied to recorded candidate lineage rather than prestige. It can name a DSEx optimizer report or research-series component without implying Pareto endorsed the project.
candidates.etymology: Uses the established Pareto term associated with Vilfredo Pareto and later optimization usage; coined compound for this portfolio.
known_concerns: Pareto can be overused as a rigor signal when no true frontier or trade-off analysis is present.
Should not become the master brand because the product is broader than Pareto selection.
notes: code_projection: hex=pareto_trace; otp=:pareto_trace; module=ParetoTrace; mix=mix pareto_trace.report; config=:pareto_trace; telemetry=[:pareto_trace, :frontier, :stop]
current_embodiment: Current embodiment can label optimizer reports that record candidates, scores, and non-dominated comparisons.
horizon_embodiment: Horizon embodiment can label artifact-optimization archive views when multiple metrics and rejected alternatives are retained.

citation_stewardship: Attribution duty is to cite Pareto only for the established frontier or efficiency concept when that concept is actually used; ambiguity or harm is prestige inflation and historical simplification; viable without the person's name as frontier_trace.

Requires citations and context when used in docs so it does not become decorative erudition.

horizon_embodiment: Horizon embodiment can carry artifact-campaign ledgers with exploratory diagnostics and promotion evidence.
